items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the composition of the board of the Niagara Frontier transportation authority
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3460

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the public authorities law, in
relation to the composition of the board of the Niagara Frontier
transportation authority

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

To provide a representative of the transit dependent community and/or
people with disabilities with voting positions on the NFTA Board of
Commissioners.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Amends subdivision 1 of Section 1299-c of the public authorities law
to provide a representative of the transit dependent community and/or
people with disabilities with voting positions on the NFTA Board of
Commissioners.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Under current law, the NFTA Board of Commissioners consists of one
chairman, ten voting members, and two non-voting members. One
nonvoting member represents the Authority's largest labor
organization, and the second non-voting member represents the transit
dependent community and/or people with disabilities. By switching this
member from a non-voting member to a voting member ensures that the
needs of the transit dependent individuals represented have a true
voice and vote when it comes to the critical matter of their mass
transit transportation.

Under this bill, the number of voting members of the Board (in
addition to the Chairman) would increase from ten to eleven. The
additional voting member would be representatives of the transit
dependent community and/or people with disabilities. The transit
dependent community and people with disabilities represent a
significant percentage of the NFTA Metro ridership base. The
appointment of this voting members will ensure that their interests
are properly represented and taken into consideration by the board.
This member would also provide real time input from those
constituencies and help the NFTA best serve and connect with riders.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2013-14 - A.3133, held in Assembly Corporations Committee
2015-2016A. 1081- Held in Assembly Corporations Committee

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This bill shall take effect on the 180th day after becoming a law.
